contracts.description: Meeting & Conference Platform HTTP API (/api/v1, /api/v2).

HTTP surface exposed by the Calling service: health, the call API (list, get, available actions), application call creation and control (accept, decline, cancel, end, hold, resume, transfer, session removal, media credentials), the endpoint registry, signaling-credential minting, the endpoint's signaling operations (WebSocket channel, offer recovery, accept / decline, media credentials), the media connection gateway (admission before every media connection) and the media provider callback; the platform credential, signaling credential, media credential and provider signature schemes; the error envelope. No generic state mutation. Protected calls (privacyRelaySessionId, PRIVACY_RELAY_V1, fail closed: PRIVACY_AUTHORIZATION_UNAVAILABLE) and the internal Privacy Relay enforcement route (POST /internal/v1/privacy-relay/enforcement). The public Privacy Relay API served by this ingress is specified by cfmeet.privacy-relay.http-api. Part E: protected public-network contact targets on POST /v1/calls (APP_TO_PSTN; PUBLIC_ROUTE_DENIED / PUBLIC_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE / TELECOM_SPEND_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) the callback relay (callbackRequested on POST /v1/calls) and the internal Telephony event receiver (POST /internal/v1/telephony/events). Part F: the enterprise calling API under /v1/enterprise/** (policies, departments, extensions, ring groups, queues, IVR, business hours, forwarding, voicemail, recording policies, audit; enterprise.* scopes, expectedVersion, VERSION_CONFLICT / ENTERPRISE_POLICY_DENIED) and enterprise call targets. 1.9.0 DCN inbound offers (POST /internal/v1/telephony/dcn-inbound-calls) and presentedNumberResourceId (Part IV L); 1.10.0 the SMS Gateway as a platform-event producer (sms.* webhooks, Part IV N).

Canonical call-domain vocabulary (Part C sections 15-25): the 17 call states, call kind, normalized failure categories, terminal reasons, participant roles, session states, endpoint categories, call event types, the call representation (CallCore / CallSummary), ring-offer, media-access, transfer and endpoint vocabularies, server-authorized media capabilities and the bounded safe event data object. Part F: VOICEMAIL_RECEIVED / VOICEMAIL_READY / VOICEMAIL_DELETED call events. Part F: ENTERPRISE_ROUTING_STEP call events (durable enterprise routing evidence).

Payload of every call event published through Calling's transactional outbox inside the cfmeet.platform.event-envelope: ids, scope, gap-free sequence, call version, states, time, correlation id and safe data. Provider-independent; no telephone numbers, provider ids, credentials or tokens.

Request and response bodies of the application-calling API (Part C sections 20-25): call creation, ring-offer answers, cancel / end / hold / resume / transfer and their results, session removal, available actions, the ring-offer and transfer representations, media credentials, endpoints, signaling credentials and offer recovery. No client-chosen scope, state, permission or provider data; no provider identifiers or administrative capabilities in responses. Part F: enterprise extension targets, enterprise transfer targets and the enterprise context of created calls. 1.5.0 presentedNumberResourceId: present an entitled Digital Communications Number on a protected-contact call (Part IV L).

Frames of an endpoint's realtime signaling channel: call signals (call.incoming ... call.invitation_expired) derived from committed state and sent after commit, with event id, call id, version / sequence, target endpoint and principal, safe state, issue time, offer expiry, correlation id and a bounded payload; and the channel control frames. No telephone numbers, provider ids, credentials or tokens. Part F: call.queued and call.queue_position (to the caller of a queued enterprise Call; data queueId, position). call.ivr_waiting / call.ivr_input (to the caller of a Call in an IVR; never the key pressed). Part F: call.recording_started (the server-issued recording notice) and call.recording_stopped. Part F: call.voicemail_started (the caller is now leaving a message). Part G: call.route_changed (a public leg failed over to another route on the same Call; data failover only).

Transport-neutral push-ready payload of a ring offer (call id, offer id, call kind, optional caller display name, issue and expiry times) for a future push service. No media credential, provider token, API credential or telephone number.

Enterprise calling bodies (Part F sections 52-62): enterprise call policy, departments, extensions, ring groups, call queues and queue entries, IVR flows and versions, business hours, forwarding rules, voicemail mailboxes and messages, call-recording policies, authorizations and recordings, administrative audit and the safe enterprise call context. Never a raw telephone number, provider / SIP identifier, DTMF digits, object key or public URL.

Shared definitions: service identity, runtime environment, request/correlation ids, UUIDs, application environment kind, principal kind, key ids, internal permissions. Part F: internal permissions telephony-leg.media (Calling -> Telephony: answer / built-in prompt / capture of internal enterprise SIP legs) telephony-enterprise.offer (Telephony -> Calling: internal enterprise SIP dialog offers and keypad input) and telephony-capture.deliver (Telephony -> Calling: edge media captures — voicemail / recording audio with integrity metadata). Part IV: platform-credential.authenticate, platform-principal.resolve, platform-principal.register, platform-identity.read and platform-identity.administer (received by Platform Access) and number-resource.read (received by Numbering). Numbering routing grant permissions (number-route.resolve, number-caller-identity.authorize, number-sms-sender.authorize, number-grant.verify). 1.8.0 number-sms-route.resolve (Part IV M). 1.9.0 number-usage.report, number-risk.report and number-relay.lease (Part IV S, T and P §§119–120). 1.9.1 cfmeet.messaging named as a service identity (Part V A).
JOSE header of internal service tokens (EdDSA pinned).
Claims of internal service tokens: issuer, exact audience, runtime environment, short lifetime, token id, signed request and correlation ids, optional delegated context.
Safe customer/application/actor identifiers carried inside a signed service token.
Receiver-controlled trust policy: trusted issuers, Ed25519 public keys and locally granted internal permissions.
Internal service-to-service HTTP conventions: service auth security scheme, request/correlation headers, normalized internal auth errors.

Envelope for durable cross-service events. Payload contracts are registered separately by the producing service (Calling: cfmeet.calling.call-lifecycle-event; Privacy Relay: cfmeet.privacy-relay.event).

Customer webhooks (Part G §68): application-scoped subscriptions (create / list / get / update / delete / rotate-secret), the safe subscription view (the signing secret is returned only on create / rotation), delivery records with dead-letter visibility and manual replay, and the normalized, signed event body (public catalog projected from committed domain events; never a provider or internal payload). Served by Calling's platform ingress. Part IV: 1.1.0 sms.received (N); 1.2.0 sms.requested / submitted / delivered / failed / unknown / blocked (O) from the SMS Gateway (references, status and codes only; never content or a number).

Usage and limits (Part G §69 / §70): the ledger of final consumption facts of the authenticated application environment (application media, public-network legs with KNOWN / ESTIMATED / UNKNOWN cost evidence, stored voicemail / recording artifacts — never a bill) and the limit status (request rate, concurrent calls, telecom spend) with every level of the API-client chain (tenant → application → service account → credential), the independent principal axis of a principal resolved in the caller's scope, and the binding level. Served by Calling's platform ingress.

Messages of the shared identity authority (Part IV Workstream B, ADR 0032): identity snapshots (tenant, application, environment, service account, credential WITHOUT verifier material, principal, scopes), credential authentication outcomes with the trusted authority chain and throttling, the trusted delegated context, credential status, authorization evaluation, the scope registry (Calling, Numbering and SMS scopes; PRIVILEGED_OPERATOR trust for numbers.admin), the commit-ordered identity change feed, Part III import receipts, principal resolution / telephone-endpoint registration / tombstones and the error envelope.

Internal HTTP surface of services/platform-access: GET /health, GET /ready and the service-authenticated /internal/v1 API — credential authentication, credential status, authorization evaluation, trusted context, identity change feed, import receipts, scope registry, principal resolution / registration / tombstone (Calling, Numbering) and operator administration (operator console, audited).

The canonical Numbering vocabulary and messages (Part IV C5, ADR 0033): Number Resource identity (CF Meet ids canonical, provider identifiers never exposed), type, capabilities with provenance, opaque provider binding references, inventory observations, reservations, DCN assignments with ownership and routing references, routing profiles, lifecycle transitions, the trusted context and the error envelope; 1.1.0 the capability and country catalog (E); 1.2.0 KYC requirements, cases, protected evidence metadata, decisions, appeals and eligibility decisions (F); 1.3.0 provider command, provider event and incident vocabularies and the provider callback acknowledgement (G). 1.4.0 inventory search results / pages with freshness, KYC indicators, country and number-type lists, reservation creation / list, hold basis and conversion, RELEASE_HOLD commands (H). 1.5.0 acquisitions, route families / configurations / readiness (I). 1.6.0 ownership and assignment requests / views, routing target kinds, pools and transfer links (J). 1.7.0 routing grant rule codes (K). 1.8.0 lifecycle stewardship messages (P–X): suspensions, releases, quarantines, reassignment, usage, risk decisions and appeals, port requests, access justification / ownership periods / verification, operational controls, reconciliation report, usage / risk-signal reports and relay import / lease / resolution (Part P); new domain rules.

Numbering domain events in the platform envelope (transactional outbox, at least once, per-aggregate order): resource discovered / lifecycle-changed / classified, binding changed, capability changed, reservation changed, assignment changed, routing profile revised, catalog revised, KYC requirements published, KYC case changed, KYC evidence received, eligibility evaluated, provider command changed, provider event received. No telephone number, provider identifier, credential or secret; 1.4.0 RELEASE_HOLD provider commands (H); 1.5.0 acquisition changed, route changed (I); 1.6.0 pool changed (J). 1.7.0 number.suspended, number.restored, release / quarantine / usage / risk / port / relay-lease changes (P–X).

HTTP surface of services/numbering: GET /health, /ready, /openapi.json (the served contract); customer reads of the caller's own DCN assignments / history / reservations, the catalog, KYC / eligibility (F); 1.4.0 provider-neutral inventory search, countries and number types, reservations (create with Idempotency-Key, list, cancel) (H); 1.5.0 acquisitions (provisioning with eligibility re-evaluation and hold read-back) and provider route configuration (I); provider callbacks (G); and the service-authenticated internal Number Resource view (/internal/v1, number-resource.read). 1.5.0 internal route view and consumer route readiness (number-route.acknowledge). 1.6.0 ownership and assignment: assignment creation / activation on proven readiness, routing revisions, employee offboarding, same-owner transfers, organizational pools and the operator assignment history (J). 1.7.0 routing grants: inbound resolution (number-route.resolve), caller-identity / SMS-sender grants (delegated scope) and authoritative verification (number-grant.verify) (K). 1.8.0 delegated current-assignment view for Calling's caller-identity policy (L). 1.9.0 dedicated SMS destination resolver (number-sms-route.resolve); inbound-resolutions is voice only (M); 1.10.0 the SMS Gateway's sender re-check on number-assignments (Part IV O). 1.11.0 inventoryClass on voice inbound resolutions, grant verifications and current-assignment views (L closure: synthetic test interconnects). 1.12.0 lifecycle stewardship (P–X) and the relay-number import / lease / resolution API (Part P).

Number routing grants (Part IV Workstream K): inbound resolution, caller-identity / SMS-sender grant requests and verification bodies, the grant claims (typ cf-number-grant+jwt, Numbering's dedicated grant key, no telephone number, revision-bound) and the receiver-authoritative grant trust bundle. 1.1.0 CurrentAssignment (L). 1.2.0 SmsDestinationResolutionRequest (M). 1.3.0 inventoryClass (SYNTHETIC / REAL) on voice resolutions, valid verifications and the current-assignment view (L closure). 1.4.0 ROUTING_DISABLED (an operator kill switch, Workstream W).

The CF Meet Privacy Relay API (Part D sections 26-30): Communication Contexts (create, list, get, typed versioned update / participant reassignment, suspend, resume, complete, revoke, privacy-safe evidence) and Privacy Relay Sessions (create, list, get, suspend, resume, revoke). Served by the authenticated platform ingress; Privacy Relay is the business and data authority. One generic model for first-party and external applications; no telephone numbers, providers, Contact Vault material or credentials.

Internal HTTP surface of services/privacy-relay: GET /health and the service-authenticated /internal/v1 API (context and session commands and reads for the platform ingress, communication authorization for protected calls). Scope only from the signed delegated platform context. 1.4.0 DCN caller protection under Numbering's routing grant (Part IV L).

Canonical Privacy Relay vocabulary: context / session lifecycles, channels, direction policy, subject references (principal id or opaque ContactReference id), relay strategies, routes, authorization decisions and reasons, enforcement states and reasons, audit event types, the bounded context policy and the error envelope.

Communication Context request and response bodies: create, typed update, lifecycle command, representation, mutation result, list and evidence. No client-chosen scope, status, version, authorization result, telephone number, provider or arbitrary policy document.
Privacy Relay Session request and response bodies: create (narrowing only), representation, mutation result and list. A session is not a call; relayIdentityBindingRef is opaque and server-owned.

Communication authorization request (Calling -> Privacy Relay) and decision: current context AND session at server time, normalized reasons, validity, decision id. No contacts, no provider ids, no client-asserted result.
Payload of every Privacy Relay outbox event (privacy-relay.* inside cfmeet.platform.event-envelope): audit event id, gap-free sequence, versions, statuses, correlation id and bounded safe data.
Privacy Relay -> Calling active-call enforcement command and result (restrictive only; deduplicated by enforcementEventId).

Contact Vault bodies (Part D sections 31-33): the raw-input create / update requests (the ONLY bodies with telephoneNumber), disable, and the safe ProtectedContact representation (masked display, country, capabilities, verification) — never a number, ciphertext, nonce, fingerprint or key version.

Contact Vault delegated access (Part D section 31): grant request / response (served by Calling, no telephone number), the Contact Vault access token claims (typ cf-contact-access+jwt, dedicated key) and the receiver-authoritative contact delegation trust bundle.

Contact Resolution Grants (Calling, protected-contact.grant-for-execution; no contact value) and Telephony-only execution resolution (protected-contact.resolve-for-execution): the only internal body that carries a canonical E.164 number.

Temporary relay-number assignment of a Privacy Relay Session (relay-number.assign): assignment id = relay identity binding, generation, country, capabilities, lifecycle. Never the number, its provider binding or the inventory id.

Inbound relay resolution (relay-number.resolve-inbound) and inbound caller protection (protected-contact.protect-inbound), Telephony only: safe mapping references and a ContactReference, never a destination or relay number in a response. 1.2.0 ProtectDcnCallerRequest / DcnCallerResult (Part IV L).

Privacy-safe call evidence of a Privacy Relay Session (served by Calling, privacy.evidence.read): canonical timing, normalized outcomes, authoritative connected duration, attempts and decision ids; never a number, provider identifier or credential.

Provider-neutral vocabulary of public-network execution (Part E): leg statuses (UNKNOWN is never a failure), public route classes, directions, end reasons, failure categories, normalized event types, bridge kinds, route health, country / currency codes. No provider, carrier, SIP or telephone-number concept. Part F: ENTERPRISE_INTERNAL legs of enterprise SIP devices; ANSWER / PROMPT (built-in prompts) on them. 1.2.0 InterconnectClass (Part IV L closure).
Normalized Telephony events delivered to Calling (leg status, bridge and usage facts) and Calling's disposition answer. CF Meet ids, normalized vocabulary and timestamps only.

Phone-to-app inbound offer from Telephony to Calling and Calling's answer (canonical Call / CallLeg). References only: never the called relay number or the caller's number. 1.1.0 DcnInboundOffer: inbound calls to Digital Communications Numbers with Numbering's grant (Part IV L). 1.2.0 DcnInboundOffer.interconnectClass (L closure).

Part F: Telephony -> Calling internal enterprise SIP dialog offers (opaque device reference, dialled short code) and transient keypad input for IVRs. Never a number, SIP URI, edge endpoint, channel id or provider identifier.

Part F: Telephony -> Calling delivery of an edge media capture (voicemail): audio with size / duration / SHA-256, or a bounded failure. Never an object key, URL, file path, channel id or provider identifier.

Calling -> Telephony commands (ORIGINATE, TERMINATE / HOLD / RESUME, BRIDGE) and their answers (leg / bridge views, the error envelope). Versioned; commandId, idempotencyKey, correlationId, Call / CallLeg / attempt / route ids, authorization evidence, spend reservation and expected generation. No caller identity, number, provider, carrier or SIP field. Part F: ENTERPRISE_INTERNAL legs of enterprise SIP devices; ANSWER / PROMPT (built-in prompts) on them. Part F: CAPTURE (edge voicemail capture into a transient spool) on them. 1.3.0 presentedIdentity: a DCN caller identity under Numbering's single-use grant (Part IV L). 1.4.0 OriginateCommand.interconnectClass (L closure: synthetic test interconnects).

Normalized route availability for Calling's Routing Engine: opaque route references with health and KNOWN / UNKNOWN evidence of capacity, cost estimate and quality. Provider-neutral. 1.1.0 RouteCandidate.interconnectClass (L closure).

Telephony's restricted provider-level usage record (one per leg; duration, billable seconds, provider cost only when known, conservative estimate otherwise, idempotency key). The fact delivered to Calling is cfmeet.telephony.event LegUsage.

HTTP surface of services/telephony: health and the provider callback ingress (provider-authenticated before parsing, 16 KiB limit, dedupe), and the service-authenticated /internal/v1 API for Calling (legs originate / get / terminate / hold / resume, bridges create / get / end, route availability, readiness). Metrics live on a separate listener. Part F: ENTERPRISE_INTERNAL legs of enterprise SIP devices; ANSWER / PROMPT (built-in prompts) on them. Part F: CAPTURE (edge voicemail capture into a transient spool) on them.

SMS Gateway vocabulary and messages (Part IV M–O): transport status, direction, encoding, control reasons, the error envelope; 1.1.0 messages, threads, provider callback acknowledgements (N); 1.2.0 send and opt-out requests (O). Remote parties are masked; no provider identifier.

HTTP surface of services/sms-gateway, served at /openapi.json: health, readiness; 1.1.0 message / thread reads (sms.read) and the inbound provider callback (N); 1.2.0 sending (sms.send, Idempotency-Key), opt-outs and delivery receipts (O).

SMS Gateway message events in the platform envelope (transactional outbox, at least once): received (N); requested, submitted, delivered, failed, unknown, blocked (O). Published to the platform customer webhook delivery as sms.*. Never content, a number or a provider identifier.

Messaging vocabulary and messages (Part V C): error envelope, security profiles, protocol and the single accepted MLS cipher suite, devices and their PUBLIC MLS material, registration challenges, KeyPackage publication, revocation, the key-transparency tree head and RFC 9162 proofs (UNWITNESSED). Never a private key, group secret, ciphertext or plaintext. 1.1.0 conversations (eight generic context classes, opaque context references, persisted security profile with MLS binding, lifecycle), the application messaging policy and its effective snapshot (Part V D). 1.2.0 signed key-transparency tree heads (log id, timestamp, Ed25519 signature, key id; Part V G.5) and the effective policy's message features (§28; platform policy version 2: SUPPORT defaults to PRIVATE_E2EE, Appendix G). 1.3.0 (Parts E-G prerequisites): members and roles, messages (PRIVATE_E2EE ciphertext with acceptance digest / MANAGED text; tombstone lifecycle), permalinks, read cursors, durable conversation events and replay pages, MLS commits / group state / KeyPackage claims / Welcomes, blocks; effective policy platform version 3; new error codes. 1.4.0 client tokens, realtime tickets, presence settings, push registrations; readiness reports the realtime gateway. 1.5.0 attachments (Attachment, AttachmentUploadIntent, AttachmentIntentRequest, AttachmentDownloadGrant) and legal holds (Part V F, G).

HTTP surface of services/messaging, served at /openapi.json: health, readiness and the device / key-directory API under /v1/messaging (Platform Access credential, scopes messages.send / messages.read, verified acting principal). 1.1.0 /v1/conversations (create with Idempotency-Key, list, get, lifecycle PATCH) and /v1/messaging/policy (Part V D). 1.2.0 tree heads in the device directory and transparency proofs are signed; without a configured signing key those routes answer 503 (never an unsigned head). 1.3.0 membership, messages, permalinks, read cursors, event replay, the MLS Delivery Service routes and blocks. 1.4.0 the realtime gateway (/v1/realtime WebSocket with single-use tickets, /v1/realtime/tickets with client tokens), client tokens and sessions, presence settings and push registrations. 1.5.0 attachment upload intents, finalization, metadata, download grants and proxied reads; legal holds.

Messaging domain events in the platform envelope (transactional outbox, at least once): messaging.device.registered, messaging.device.key-packages-published, messaging.device.revoked. No key material, ciphertext or content. 1.1.0 messaging.conversation.created, messaging.conversation.lifecycle-changed, messaging.conversation.updated, messaging.policy.updated. 1.2.0 message, member, read-cursor and MLS welcome events (ids, sequences, states only). 1.3.0 messaging.client-session.revoked.

Messaging realtime WebSocket protocol v1 (Part V Part E): client frames (subscribe, unsubscribe, ack, typing, presence.set, presence.query, auth.refresh, ping) and server frames (welcome, subscribed, event, sync.required, subscription.revoked, typing, presence, presence.snapshot, device.event, server.draining, error …), close codes and compatibility rules. Durable events reference the ConversationEvent of cfmeet.messaging.common; no plaintext of PRIVATE_E2EE conversations ever appears.
